Eggs and Flies

By: Joy Summers | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Where do the eggs you buy on the supermarket shelf come from. We investigate NULAID EGGS

Unique Selling Point:
ANGRY NEIGHBOURS, A RECALCITRANT CORPORATE, UNHAPPY CHICKENS AND FOOTAGE ALREADY TAKEN IF ALL ELSE FAILS

Summary:
You may not have heard of Quantum foods but they are a company with a market cap of a billion rand, listed on the JSE. A share will cost you R5,50, and according to their latest results this farming company earned R2, 6 billion rand in 2021 with an operating profit of R74 million.

What you may have heard of, is one of their brands- NULAID eggs. Because you will likely find them at your friendly Spar and Pick and Pay who buy their eggs from this supplier, and promises them and you, an impressive list of values that determine how they operate.

According to NULAID’s website, listed under their values is respect for the dignity of their people, and the products that are brought to market are affordable, produced using up to date technology and production facilities.

And excellence must be a way of life they say. Every task in their business will be performed in a superior manner and they will communicate regularly with their customers, their shareholders and their people.

What they don’t say and why we are scratching around in the manure, is that they don’t communicate well with their neighbor’s and the welfare of the chickens that produce their eggs – appears to be an afterthought, or no thought at all.

HEKPOORT

Nulaid has several different properties that produce eggs. But it’s at Hekpoort that we find a stink and millions of flies that have gotten up the noses and in the coffee of NULAID’S neighbors.

Here they have 10 chicken houses each holding 22 000 birds. All in all 220 000 birds laying eggs for your morning breakfast.





Further information:
Carte Blanche has visited laying farms in the past. They are generally unpleasant places if you are one of those softies that cares about animal welfare. 2 to 3 Chickens spend around 18 months stuffed into tiny wire cages where they can’t even turn around comfortably to take a drink from the drip line. But the laying farm that Carte Blanche visited and filmed in 2020 was run by a fastidious Dutchman, and at least it was clean, and there wasn’t a fly to be seen and the chickens could eat to their hearts content. Drip lines worked.

Now let’s go to Nulaid’s facility in Hekpoort, where the neighbors are gearing up for a fight with Quantum foods and are determined to close it down. Millions of flies are everywhere – inside and outside the chicken houses. The drip line was not properly repaired and wet manure lies all over the place. Chicken carcasses are hastily buried, whereas in other egg production places – carcasses are frozen and then given to lion or other facilities.

Vivien Law is a neighbor who is at her wits end. Her home is a fly infested hell, but despite a myriad complaints. Mike Crewe Brown is another neighbour, his once thriving organic cooking school called Wickedearth foods is struggling. Customers hate the flies, and so does he. He has years of emails fighting with his neighbors but they don’t seem to act. Other local people who live close by, find flies in their coffee on a regular basis. That Nulaid has become a health hazard for the surrounding people and the dying chickens (its recorded in their annual statement) is not in question, but are you comfortable as a consumer buying your eggs from such an outfit. Okay so eggs have a protective shell, so you are protected by the miracle that is an egg, produced for you by a chicken that will be lucky to survive NULAIDS facility- but will Pick and Pay and Spar really want to see their egg supplier on Carte Blanche – for all the wrong reasons? And aren’t we supposed to be more careful about zoonotic diseases in the age of a Pandemic that came from an animal?

Script:


Final Script Nulaid’s Flies for TX Sunday 28th November 2021 for Voice over

Voice over One
This is one of Nulaid’s chicken farms on the outskirts of Gauteng. It’s a subsidiary of Quantum foods, listed on the JSE.

Quantum earned revenue of R2.4 billion rand last year, and you may have helped it do that by buying some of its eggs. Because Nulaid is a big supplier to Checkers and Pick and Pay.

Only Nulaid has a problem. In this Hekpoort valley it’s angered neighbors and crippled surrounding businesses, because Nulaid aren’t just producing eggs here, it may also be producing a plague of flies.

Up sound Buzzing flies

Lance Quidding
I am sitting here with tears in my eyes. With staff coming to me with babies in their arms with flies in their mouths. WHAT CAN WE DO! We are desperate, desperate, desperate.

Voice over Two
Believing that Nulaid has been deaf to their cries, the community eventually called us.

Vivien Law
Well, the trust is broken because they've been arrogant, and as far as I'm concerned, they are the epitome of unconscious capitalists

Voice over Three
Vivien Law is one of Nulaid’s direct neighbours. She’s planted olive and Pecan trees and supplements her income with accommodation. But now she is thinking of giving it all up, because she finds herself raising her children in a fly infested hell.

Up sound Vivien
This is our tv room, and I just want you to have a look at the windowsill. These are just the flies just trying to get in crazy hey.....disgusting
Vivien
We have to clear this out every couple of days

Vivien
I mean, the other morning, I went out the back door and it was about 6:15 in the morning and it was going to be a warm day and there was just a cloud of black over the olive trees at the back of the farm. And in all seriousness, you go to the toilet in the morning and you have to have one of these because it's like riding a horse, you got to slap your arse the whole time to keep the flies off!

Mac
And you are not even being kinky!
NO! They laugh


Voice over Four
And the fly strips and screens barely make a difference – even indoors

Vivien
I cleaned out the other day after four days of leaving it on and this...
Mac interrupts
Is that flies?!
Vivien
Look at this these are dead flies..
Mac groans
Vivien
This whole bottle here is four days collected in there
Mac
I can’t deal with this!

Voice over Five
Across the road at a cucumber farm where Christina Motlhamme works – it’s the same story

Christina
If you lie in bed and look up at the ceiling, there are just flies. Just flies.
My children are scared to visit here, because they know there are a lot of flies.

Voice over Six
Even making a cup of coffee can be hazardous to your health

Christina
The flies get into my coffee. YASSIS. I was so cross!

Voice over seven
Lance Quiding is an aquaponics farmer and grows lettuce on Nulaid’s western border

LANCE
My staff can't sleep. I've lost staff members because of the unbearable conditions with the flies when they cook. It's really thick, thick, thick with flies. So it impacts our business through the people that we employ more than anything else.

Voice over eight
But Nulaid’s flies are an old problem. Mike Crewe- Brown is also at loggerheads with the company. In 2012 the community got permission to visit the farm, where Mike took these pictures of open bins of rotting eggs.

There were flies then, there are flies now, and his organic cooking school has had massive cancellations

MIKE
We have already lost jobs, we used to have 10 laborers, we are down to two.

Voice over nine
For years the community has documented how Nulaid has left piles of chicken manure lying in the sun for weeks where flies breed.

LINK
Eventually by 2015 the state vet made some recommendations- the company says they are implementing them. But surrounding farms and businesses don’t agree

Voice over ten
The small scale farmers and lodges here say Nulaid is a corporate farm that denies and deflects blame, and only does minimum damage control when they complain.

Vivien
This one here. Look at this. This is one week and its full.

Voice over eleven
Late last year Nulaid invited Mike and Vivien for a site visit with their vet. But Nulaid covered over a soggy pit of manure unbeknown even to their own vet

Mike
And next minute the vet fell literally hip deep, which is recorded in his report into a wet pit of chicken faeces.

Voice over twelve
Nulaid has since removed the open bins, but the bird carcasses are still thrown into pits in the ground called Mortality pits, and soggy piles of manure are said to wait days outside for collection. Yet Nulaid claim on their website they use up to date technology and production facilities.

Vivien
I charged over there in my gumboots the other day to go and see where all these flies were coming from and what I saw was shocking.
MAC
what does it look like inside there?
Vivien
No, it's horrible, its just ...

Voice over thirteen
By the time Vivien got there the manure had been removed, and all that was left over was this sludge

Vivian up sound
And this has supposedly been removed?


Mac
Did you see the maggots?
Vivien
Yes, I saw the maggots inside the house and outside the house, and then just above where all the sludge is there was a thick layer of tiny little flies that had just hatched.
Mac
Groans
Vivien
I am so sorry.

Voice over fourteen
The only way to find out what it looked like inside was to go in undercover ourselves.

Up sound buzzing

These birds have been crammed inside these cages for four weeks. They will be here another 17 months laying eggs.

It’s hot and there were flies in the manure below the chickens. The drippers in some of the houses are allegedly broken so water gets into the manure where maggots soon become flies

Nulaid says all hens are kept within the code of practice from the South African Poultry Association. Nulaid conducted an internal fly control audit on the 17th of November and it says that its audits confirm that it does not exacerbate the fly activity.

We filmed these visuals two days later.

Amos Selaledi
We can’t afford not to be compliant because we are listed!

Voice over fifteen
On the 19th November Quantum’s executive for layers, Amos Selaledi met community members

Chanelle at meeting
I can’t understand how you can even supply PNP and checkers. I was there the drains weren’t working, the place was falling apart !

Voice over Sixteen
Checkers has not responded to our request for comment. Pick N Pay says that it doesn’t buy eggs from Hekpoort farm because those eggs are ungraded. After our visit Nulaid put up these buckets along the road, and began to clean up. Pick N Pay arrived a couple of days later and said they were satisfied with the fly control programme. But the community are not convinced

Up sound
I think if you send in the health inspector today they would close you down.

Voice over seventeen
After the meeting Amos Selaledi agreed to speak to our producer in an impromptu interview

Amos
You must remember we are in the food business and food and flies don’t go together
So we need to ensure that whatever we do complies to the food standard.
Joy
And do they?
Pause
Yes they do. But like I said things tend to go wrong.

Commentary eighteen
But why it’s been going wrong here for so long, is not clear.

Nulaid admits the farm is old but says its maintenance programme is up to standard.

Joy Summers
What is missing is a very specific time frame, do you not have that?
Amos Seleledi
The specific timeframes I gave was to do away with mortality pits, do away with manure pile ups, to address the fly control programmes. I said those three at the latest second or 3rd week of December

Voice over nineteen
As the meeting progressed, Nulaid suggested they bring in an independent auditor. But the community clamored for an unplanned visit that same afternoon

Amos
Let the health inspector come
Francois
Why don’t we let Carte Blanche in I am sure your customers are quite keen to see what your facility is like! What are you hiding?
Amos Seleledi
No, no, no there is nothing to hide
Francois
Ok then let’s go.
Amos
I am making a decision, I am not going to allow Carte Blanche in our premises that is not the purpose of why I am here.

Voice over twenty
Nulaid says its consulting vet went to the farm on Thursday for what it called an unannounced visit. Here’s what he found: despite a few breakthrough spots, Nulaid’s fly control measures inside the houses were effective, there were significantly more flies outside than inside the houses, and that there were fewer fly-breeding areas and maggot spots than on previous inspections. He also claims the flies could be coming from other areas, including an informal settlement we were told is 2.5km away. After conducting four other audits this week, Nulaid claims it’s operating within the required standards.

Amos Selaledi
I can reassure consumers that the product you are getting on your shelf comes from facilities that complies with animal welfare, with the health regulations, and also with our biosecurity protocol

THE END 10 01.

PROMO’S

PROMO ONE 11 seconds
A Hekpoort community says that a listed food company is a source of flies and destroying their livelihoods. Not so, says the company who went into damage control this week

PROMO TWO
Why did a listed factory farm producing eggs for some of our largest retailer refuse to let us into their facility

Francois
Why don’t we let Carte Blanche in I am sure your customers are quite keen to see what your facility is like! What are you hiding?
Amos Seleledi
No, no, no there is nothing to hide
Francois
Ok then let’s go.
Amos
I am making a decision, I am not going to allow Carte Blanche in our premises that is not the purpose of why I am here.

PROMO THREE
A listed food company is at loggerheads with a local community over a plague of flies

Mac
Did you see the maggots?
Vivien
Yes, I saw the maggots inside the house and outside the house, and then just above where all the sludge is there was a thick layer of tiny little flies that had just hatched.
Mac
Groans
Vivien
I am so sorry.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Where do the eggs you buy on the supermarket shelf come from. We investigate NULAID EGGS
metadata.Unique Selling Point: ANGRY NEIGHBOURS, A RECALCITRANT CORPORATE, UNHAPPY CHICKENS AND FOOTAGE ALREADY TAKEN IF ALL ELSE FAILS
metadata.Summary: You may not have heard of Quantum foods but they are a company with a market cap of a billion rand, listed on the JSE. A share will cost you R5,50, and according to their latest results this farming company earned R2, 6 billion rand in 2021 with an operating profit of R74 million. What you may have heard of, is one of their brands- NULAID eggs. Because you will likely find them at your friendly Spar and Pick and Pay who buy their eggs from this supplier, and promises them and you, an impressive list of values that determine how they operate. According to NULAID’s website, listed under their values is respect for the dignity of their people, and the products that are brought to market are affordable, produced using up to date technology and production facilities. And excellence must be a way of life they say. Every task in their business will be performed in a superior manner and they will communicate regularly with their customers, their shareholders and their people. What they don’t say and why we are scratching around in the manure, is that they don’t communicate well with their neighbor’s and the welfare of the chickens that produce their eggs – appears to be an afterthought, or no thought at all. HEKPOORT Nulaid has several different properties that produce eggs. But it’s at Hekpoort that we find a stink and millions of flies that have gotten up the noses and in the coffee of NULAID’S neighbors. Here they have 10 chicken houses each holding 22 000 birds. All in all 220 000 birds laying eggs for your morning breakfast.
metadata.Further information: Carte Blanche has visited laying farms in the past. They are generally unpleasant places if you are one of those softies that cares about animal welfare. 2 to 3 Chickens spend around 18 months stuffed into tiny wire cages where they can’t even turn around comfortably to take a drink from the drip line. But the laying farm that Carte Blanche visited and filmed in 2020 was run by a fastidious Dutchman, and at least it was clean, and there wasn’t a fly to be seen and the chickens could eat to their hearts content. Drip lines worked. Now let’s go to Nulaid’s facility in Hekpoort, where the neighbors are gearing up for a fight with Quantum foods and are determined to close it down. Millions of flies are everywhere – inside and outside the chicken houses. The drip line was not properly repaired and wet manure lies all over the place. Chicken carcasses are hastily buried, whereas in other egg production places – carcasses are frozen and then given to lion or other facilities. Vivien Law is a neighbor who is at her wits end. Her home is a fly infested hell, but despite a myriad complaints. Mike Crewe Brown is another neighbour, his once thriving organic cooking school called Wickedearth foods is struggling. Customers hate the flies, and so does he. He has years of emails fighting with his neighbors but they don’t seem to act. Other local people who live close by, find flies in their coffee on a regular basis. That Nulaid has become a health hazard for the surrounding people and the dying chickens (its recorded in their annual statement) is not in question, but are you comfortable as a consumer buying your eggs from such an outfit. Okay so eggs have a protective shell, so you are protected by the miracle that is an egg, produced for you by a chicken that will be lucky to survive NULAIDS facility- but will Pick and Pay and Spar really want to see their egg supplier on Carte Blanche – for all the wrong reasons? And aren’t we supposed to be more careful about zoonotic diseases in the age of a Pandemic that came from an animal?
